input.question: How do dead pixel fixers work?
input.ground_truth: When these pixel fixers work, it's because the pixel is stuck, and not dead. My understanding of it is, the signal telling the pixel to change color, never reaches the destination. What the fixers do, is change the color rapidly so that the signals are, in a way, forced to the pixel, so over a long period of time (an hour or two, I think) the pixel becomes unstuck, and will function as normal.

Question: How do dead pixel fixers work?

Okay! Imagine your screen is like a big grid of tiny lights, like a bunch of tiny flashlights all working together to show you pictures and videos.

Sometimes, one of these tiny lights stops working. It’s like if one flashlight in the grid doesn’t turn on, so you see a little black dot called a “dead pixel.”

A dead pixel fixer is like a magic trick that tries to make that flashlight turn back on. It shows special patterns or flashes bright colors, hoping to wake up that sleepy flashlight. Sometimes it works, and the dead pixel comes back to life! But sometimes, the flashlight just stays asleep.

So, a dead pixel fixer is like trying to wake up a sleepy light on your screen.
